content.title: What is Java?
content.description: Java is a high-level, object-oriented, platform-independent programming language developed by Sun Microsystems (now Oracle). It is widely used for developing web, desktop, mobile, and enterprise applications.

content.content: Java was introduced in 1995 with the philosophy 'Write Once, Run Anywhere (WORA)'. Java programs are compiled into bytecode, which runs on the Java Virtual Machine (JVM), making Java platform-independent.

content.title: Why Learn Java?
content.content: Java is one of the most popular programming languages because of its simplicity, security, portability, and strong community support.
Java provides several powerful features that make it suitable for building reliable and scalable applications.

items.question: Platform Independent
items.answer: Java programs run on any system that has a JVM.

items.question: Object-Oriented
items.answer: Everything in Java revolves around objects and classes.

items.question: Secure
items.answer: Java provides built-in security features such as bytecode verification and runtime checks.

items.question: Robust
items.answer: Automatic memory management and exception handling make Java reliable.

content.content: The Java platform consists of three important components that work together to execute Java programs.

content.title: JDK
content.description: The Java Development Kit (JDK) contains tools required to develop, compile, and run Java applications.

content.title: JRE
content.description: The Java Runtime Environment (JRE) provides the libraries and runtime needed to execute Java applications.

content.title: JVM
content.description: The Java Virtual Machine (JVM) executes Java bytecode and enables platform independence.

content.content: The first Java program traditionally prints Hello, World! to the console. Every Java application starts execution from the main() method.

content.title: Hello World Program

content.content: Java is used across multiple domains due to its reliability, scalability, and portability.

content.title: Industry Usage
content.content: Java powers millions of enterprise applications in banking, healthcare, e-commerce, and cloud computing.

content.title: Universal Language Translator
content.content: Imagine writing a letter in a universal language that can be translated and understood by people from any country. Similarly, Java bytecode is understood by the JVM on any operating system.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Interviewers often begin Java interviews by asking about JDK, JRE, JVM, platform independence, and Java's key features.

items.question: Why doesn't the program run?
items.answer: The filename must exactly match the public class name.

items.question: What is a common beginner mistake?
items.answer: Forgetting to write the main() method.

items.question: Why is Java called platform-independent?
items.answer: Because bytecode runs on the JVM instead of directly on the operating system.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: JDK is used for development, JRE provides the runtime environment, and JVM executes Java bytecode.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Java is an object-oriented programming language.
Java follows Write Once, Run Anywhere.
JVM executes bytecode on different operating systems.
JDK contains JRE, and JRE contains JVM.

content.question: Why is Java called platform-independent?
options: Bytecode runs on JVM across platforms
content.answer: Bytecode runs on JVM across platforms
